state._finite.summary:
Use this type/finiteness gate before a field-specific range check.
Boolean values are rejected even though bool is an int subclass.
state._finite.see: state.PhysicsParameters : Apply physical range checks after finiteness validation.
state._finite.example:
>>> from state import _finite
>>> _finite('mass', 1.0) is None
True
>>> _finite('mass', True)
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: mass must be a finite number

state.PhysicsParameters.summary:
Create one parameter object per fixed-timestep trajectory. Its frozen
fields separate physical constants from the mutable circle state.
state.PhysicsParameters.see: state.Box.validate_for : Check that a box accommodates the chosen radius.
state.PhysicsParameters.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> p = PhysicsParameters(restitution=0, dt=0.01)
>>> (p.restitution, p.dt, p.gravity)
(0, 0.01, 9.81)

state.Box.summary:
Dimensions define the floor and displayed sides. The height participates
in geometry validation but does not create a ceiling collision.
state.Box.see: contacts.resolve_contacts : Apply floor and side-wall bounds to a state.
state.Box.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> box = Box(width=2, height=1)
>>> box.validate_for(PhysicsParameters(radius=0.2)) is None
True

state.Box.validate_for.summary:
Call this after selecting both geometry and radius. A box can be valid
on its own while too small for a particular circle.
state.Box.validate_for.see: state.Box : Validate positive dimensions independently of radius.
state.Box.validate_for.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> Box(width=0.4).validate_for(PhysicsParameters())
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: box width and height must exceed the circle diameter

state.CircleState.summary:
Store the center and velocity for in-place advancement. Construction
checks numeric state, while later field assignments remain mutable.
state.CircleState.see: integration.complete_step : Advance this state and then resolve contacts.
state.CircleState.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> state = CircleState(y=0.1, vy=2)
>>> (state.y, state.vy, state.step_count)
(0.1, 2, 0)

state.CircleState.validate.summary:
Recheck a state after manual mutation. This tests scalar validity and
the step count, without projecting coordinates onto any boundary.
state.CircleState.validate.see: contacts.resolve_contacts : Correct geometric overlap after validation.
state.CircleState.validate.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> state = CircleState()
>>> state.step_count = -1
>>> state.validate()
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
ValueError: step_count must be a nonnegative integer

state.CircleState.time.summary:
Elapsed time is reconstructed from the count and the supplied timestep;
changing dt retrospectively changes this reported time.
state.CircleState.time.see: integration.step : Increment the count during a contact-free step.

state.PhysicsParameters.__post_init__.summary:
Dataclass construction invokes this hook automatically. Recalling the
hook performs the same validation without advancing simulation time.
state.PhysicsParameters.__post_init__.see: state.PhysicsParameters : Construct the object and trigger this validation.
state.PhysicsParameters.__post_init__.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> value = PhysicsParameters()
>>> value.__post_init__() is None
True

state.Box.__post_init__.summary:
Dataclass construction invokes this hook automatically. Recalling the
hook performs the same validation without advancing simulation time.
state.Box.__post_init__.see: state.Box : Construct the object and trigger this validation.
state.Box.__post_init__.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> value = Box()
>>> value.__post_init__() is None
True

state.CircleState.__post_init__.summary:
Dataclass construction invokes this hook automatically. Recalling the
hook performs the same validation without advancing simulation time.
state.CircleState.__post_init__.see: state.CircleState : Construct the object and trigger this validation.
state.CircleState.__post_init__.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> value = CircleState()
>>> value.__post_init__() is None
True

integration.step.summary:
Use this integrator for contact-free motion and analytical comparisons.
Boundary correction belongs to complete_step, not this operation.
integration.step.see: integration.complete_step : Integrate and resolve boundary contacts.

integration.complete_step.summary:
This is the scheduler's physical timestep: first integrate, then apply
endpoint contact response, with exactly one step-count increment.
integration.complete_step.see:
integration.step : Advance without contacts.
contacts.resolve_contacts : Apply response without advancing time.
integration.complete_step.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from integration import complete_step
>>> state = CircleState(y=0.2, vy=-1, vx=0)
>>> records = complete_step(state, PhysicsParameters(dt=0.01), Box())
>>> (state.y, round(state.vy, 6), state.step_count)
(0.2, 0.87848, 1)
>>> [record.surface for record in records]
['floor']

contacts.ContactRecord.summary:
A record distinguishes touching/projection from a velocity-changing
impact. Normal signs are defined relative to each allowed half-plane.
contacts.ContactRecord.see: contacts.resolve_contacts : Create records while mutating circle state.
contacts.ContactRecord.example:
>>> from contacts import ContactRecord
>>> record = ContactRecord('floor', (0.0, 0.05), 2.0, 2.0)
>>> (record.position_correction, record.is_impact)
((0.0, 0.05), False)

contacts.ContactRecord.is_impact.summary:
Use this flag to count velocity-changing responses. A nonzero position
correction alone does not make the recorded contact an impact.
contacts.ContactRecord.is_impact.see: contacts.resolve_contacts : Record normal velocities before and after response.
contacts.ContactRecord.is_impact.example:
>>> from contacts import ContactRecord
>>> ContactRecord('floor', (0.0, 0.05), 2.0, 2.0).is_impact
False
>>> ContactRecord('floor', (0.0, 0.0), -2.0, 1.6).is_impact
True

contacts.resolve_contacts.summary:
Use direct resolution to project an overlapping state without a timestep.
Separating overlaps are corrected without reversing the outgoing velocity.
contacts.resolve_contacts.see: integration.complete_step : Integrate first, then call this resolver.

cli.finite_number.summary:
This conversion rejects NaN and infinity before option-specific range
checks. It parses numeric text rather than evaluating expressions.
cli.finite_number.see:
cli.timestep_value : Require a finite positive time.
cli.restitution_value : Require a coefficient in the closed unit interval.
cli.finite_number.example:
>>> from cli import finite_number
>>> finite_number('1e-3')
0.001
>>> finite_number('nan')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
argparse.ArgumentTypeError: must be finite

cli.restitution_value.summary:
The parser accepts both perfectly inelastic and elastic endpoints.
Coefficients outside this interval are rejected before simulation setup.
cli.restitution_value.example:
>>> from cli import restitution_value
>>> [restitution_value(text) for text in ('0', '0.8', '1')]
[0.0, 0.8, 1.0]

cli.timestep_value.summary:
The same positive-time converter serves dt and the two durations.
Whole-step alignment is checked separately for figure experiments.
cli.timestep_value.see: validation.whole_steps : Check duration alignment and workload limits.
cli.timestep_value.example:
>>> from cli import timestep_value
>>> timestep_value('0.01')
0.01
>>> timestep_value('0')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
argparse.ArgumentTypeError: must be greater than zero seconds

cli.parse_args.summary:
Figure mode extends the shared physics options with output and duration
settings; parsing validates setup without generating files or opening a GUI.
cli.parse_args.see:
main.main : Dispatch parsed GUI options.
make_figures.main : Dispatch parsed figure options.
cli.parse_args.example:
>>> from cli import parse_args
>>> args = parse_args('Example', ['--dt', '0.02', '--duration', '0.2'], figures=True)
>>> (args.dt, args.duration, args.bounce_duration, args.output_dir)
(0.02, 0.2, 10.0, 'figures')

main.main.summary:
Parsing finishes before the renderer is imported. This permits help and
invalid-option checks in a process that never opens a native window.
main.main.example:
Help can be inspected without opening a window.

>>> import contextlib, io
>>> from main import main
>>> output = io.StringIO()
>>> with contextlib.redirect_stdout(output):
...     try:
...         main(['--help'])
...     except SystemExit as exc:
...         status = exc.code
>>> (status, '--restitution' in output.getvalue())
(0, True)

make_figures.main.summary:
The returned status summarizes the generated report. File-writing
failures and failed numerical checks produce a nonzero status.
make_figures.main.example:
Help can be inspected without generating files.

>>> import contextlib, io
>>> from make_figures import main
>>> output = io.StringIO()
>>> with contextlib.redirect_stdout(output):
...     try:
...         main(['--help'])
...     except SystemExit as exc:
...         status = exc.code
>>> (status, '--restitution' in output.getvalue())
(0, True)

rendering.FixedStepScheduler.summary:
Supply elapsed wall-clock intervals while keeping the physical timestep
fixed. The scheduler owns bookkeeping but shares the supplied state.
rendering.FixedStepScheduler.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from rendering import FixedStepScheduler
>>> scheduler = FixedStepScheduler(CircleState(), PhysicsParameters(dt=0.1), Box())
>>> scheduler.advance(0.04)
0
>>> scheduler.advance(0.06)
1
>>> scheduler.state.step_count
1

rendering.FixedStepScheduler.__post_init.summary:
Construction validates the shared references before any elapsed interval
is consumed. It does not make a private copy of the mutable circle.
rendering.FixedStepScheduler.__post_init.see:
state.CircleState.validate : Check numeric state fields.
state.Box.validate_for : Check diameter-dependent geometry.
rendering.FixedStepScheduler.__post_init.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from rendering import FixedStepScheduler
>>> scheduler = FixedStepScheduler(CircleState(), PhysicsParameters(), Box())
>>> scheduler.__post_init__() is None
True
>>> scheduler.state.step_count
0

rendering.FixedStepScheduler.advance.summary:
Elapsed time can fund several fixed steps or only a fractional remainder.
The work cap bounds each call and permanently discards excess whole steps.
rendering.FixedStepScheduler.advance.see: integration.complete_step : Execute each available physical timestep.
rendering.FixedStepScheduler.advance.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from rendering import FixedStepScheduler
>>> scheduler = FixedStepScheduler(CircleState(), PhysicsParameters(dt=0.01), Box())
>>> scheduler.advance(1.2575)
60
>>> (scheduler.discarded_steps, round(scheduler.accumulator, 4))
(65, 0.0075)

rendering.RenderingDependencyError.summary:
This exception identifies missing renderer dependencies that the GUI
entry point converts into a user-facing installation message and status 1.
rendering.RenderingDependencyError.see: main.main : Handle this exception at the GUI entry point.
rendering.RenderingDependencyError.example:
>>> from rendering import RenderingDependencyError
>>> error = RenderingDependencyError('Install PyVista/VTK')
>>> (str(error), error.args)
('Install PyVista/VTK', ('Install PyVista/VTK',))

rendering.run_simulation.summary:
The GUI constructs its own default circle and box, then passes measured
elapsed time to the fixed-step scheduler until the native loop terminates.
rendering.run_simulation.see:
rendering.FixedStepScheduler : Schedule physics without owning a GUI.
main.main : Parse options and launch this renderer.
rendering.run_simulation.example:
Interactive example (manual only; opens a native window and blocks until
closed with q, Escape, or the close button; not executed by doctest)::

    from rendering import run_simulation
    from state import PhysicsParameters
    run_simulation(PhysicsParameters(restitution=0.5))

validation.whole_steps.summary:
Duration alignment is checked in units of dt with a small roundoff
allowance. Requests are rejected rather than silently shortening a run.
validation.whole_steps.see: validation.validate_experiments : Validate the three experiment step counts.

validation.validate_experiments.summary:
Coarse and fine free fall must share endpoints and remain above the
floor. Bouncing may include contacts but obeys the same step-count limit.
validation.validate_experiments.see: validation.whole_steps : Convert each requested interval to a bounded count.

validation.tolerance.summary:
This budget applies to residuals after subtracting the expected discrete
formula. It does not bound trajectory error against continuous dynamics.
validation.tolerance.see: validation.check_close : Apply an absolute allowance to a residual.
validation.tolerance.example:
>>> from validation import tolerance
>>> tolerance(1e-10, 480, 10) == 1e-10
True

validation.check_close.summary:
Checks are accumulated as data so a failed comparison need not stop
later diagnostics or figure generation.
validation.check_close.see: validation.check_true : Record a boolean condition in the same check list.
validation.check_close.example:
>>> from validation import check_close
>>> checks = []
>>> check_close(checks, 'height', 0.2, 0.2, 1e-12)
>>> (checks[0]['residual'], checks[0]['passed'])
(0.0, True)

validation.check_true.summary:
Boolean diagnostics share the report's check list with numerical
residual checks and contribute to the final passed/failed status.
validation.check_true.see: validation.check_close : Record a numerical residual comparison.
validation.check_true.example:
>>> from validation import check_true
>>> checks = []
>>> check_true(checks, 'bounded', True)
>>> checks[0]['passed']
True

validation.energy.summary:
Kinetic energy uses both velocity components; gravitational potential
uses center height relative to y=0.
validation.energy.see: validation.sample : Record this energy alongside state and time.
validation.energy.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from validation import energy
>>> round(energy(CircleState(vx=0, vy=0), PhysicsParameters()), 2)
19.62

validation.sample.summary:
The result is a new dictionary of scalar values. Later circle mutation
does not retrospectively change a previously collected sample.
validation.sample.see: validation.energy : Compute the sample's mechanical energy.
validation.sample.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from validation import sample
>>> state = CircleState()
>>> row = sample(state, PhysicsParameters())
>>> state.y = 3
>>> (row['y'], row['time'], state.y)
(2.0, 0.0, 3)

validation.free_fall.summary:
The contact-free trajectory supplies measured values; analytical and
discrete formulas supply references for signed-error and drift checks.
validation.free_fall.see: validation.run_validation : Compare coarse and fine runs at matching times.
validation.free_fall.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from validation import free_fall
>>> checks = []
>>> run = free_fall(PhysicsParameters(dt=0.1), 1, checks, 'example')
>>> (len(run['samples']), round(run['final']['y'], 4))
(2, 9.9019)
>>> all(check['passed'] for check in checks)
True

validation.bouncing.summary:
Contact records separate restitution loss from the potential-energy
change introduced by boundary projection.
validation.bouncing.example:
>>> from state import Box, CircleState, PhysicsParameters
>>> from validation import bouncing
>>> checks = []
>>> run = bouncing(PhysicsParameters(dt=0.01), 2, checks, 'example')
>>> (len(run['samples']), run['impact_counts']['floor'])
(3, 0)
>>> all(check['passed'] for check in checks)
True

validation.contact_direction.summary:
An upward floor overlap separates geometric correction from impact
response. The faulty velocity is an illustration, not a production mutation.
validation.contact_direction.see: contacts.resolve_contacts : Apply the actual direction-conditional response.
validation.contact_direction.example:
>>> from validation import contact_direction
>>> checks = []
>>> result = contact_direction(checks)
>>> (result['measured_y'], result['measured_correct_vy'], result['correct_is_impact'])
(0.2, 2.0, False)

validation.regression_checks.summary:
Only integration and contact suites are loaded here. CLI and scheduling
checks remain separate entry scripts.
validation.regression_checks.see: validation.run_validation : Include this suite result in a numerical report.
validation.regression_checks.example:
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
>>> from validation import regression_checks
>>> with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
...     result = regression_checks(Path(directory))
...     exists = (Path(directory) / 'regression_checks.txt').is_file()
>>> (result['tests_run'], result['passed'], exists)
(11, True, True)

validation.write_plots.summary:
Plotting consumes already-collected report data. Styling and file output
do not rerun the integrator or alter its recorded samples.
validation.write_plots.see: validation.run_validation : Collect a complete report before plotting.
validation.write_plots.example:
Use an existing report to write plots into a second temporary directory.
Both directories are removed after the example.

>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
>>> from validation import run_validation, write_plots
>>> with TemporaryDirectory() as data_dir, TemporaryDirectory() as plot_dir:
...     report = run_validation(data_dir, 0.8, 0.02, 0.2, 0.2)
...     saved = write_plots(report, Path(plot_dir))
...     exists = all((Path(plot_dir) / name).is_file() for name in saved)
>>> (len(saved), exists)
(4, True)

validation.write_plots.save.summary:
This closure shares the output directory and filename list with its
parent. A successful save records the name only after closing the figure.
validation.write_plots.save.see: validation.write_plots : Own the output path, report data and saved-name list.
validation.write_plots.save.example:
This example writes into a temporary directory and removes it afterwards.

>>> from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from validation import run_validation
>>> with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
...     report = run_validation(directory, 0.8, 0.02, 0.2, 0.2)
...     png_count = len(list(Path(directory).glob('*.png')))
>>> (report['status'], png_count)
('passed', 4)

validation.run_validation.summary:
This orchestrator combines regressions, trajectories, energy accounting
and plots into one report with explicit status and environment metadata.
validation.run_validation.see: make_figures.main : Convert the report status into a command exit code.
validation.run_validation.example:
This example writes into a temporary directory and removes it afterwards.

>>> from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from validation import run_validation
>>> with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
...     report = run_validation(directory, 0.8, 0.02, 0.2, 0.2)
...     png_count = len(list(Path(directory).glob('*.png')))
>>> (report['status'], png_count)
('passed', 4)

check_cli.CliChecks.summary:
The inherited unittest lifecycle runs these cases individually or as a
suite. Local fixtures exercise CLI dispatch and headless output.
check_cli.CliChecks.see: unittest.TestCase : Provide assertion methods and test lifecycle.
check_cli.CliChecks.example:
>>> import unittest
>>> from check_cli import CliChecks
>>> suite = unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(CliChecks)
>>> suite.countTestCases()
9

check_cli.CliChecks.test_defaults.summary:
Parser defaults are checked without launching either entry point, so
this case isolates the public command-line configuration.
check_cli.CliChecks.test_defaults.see: check_cli.CliChecks : Collect the related regression cases.
check_cli.CliChecks.test_defaults.example:
Run this individual regression through unittest; assertion failures are
recorded in the result rather than printed as expected output.

>>> import contextlib, io, unittest
>>> from check_cli import CliChecks
>>> result = unittest.TestResult()
>>> with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
...     _ = CliChecks('test_defaults').run(result)
>>> (result.testsRun, result.wasSuccessful())
(1, True)

check_cli.CliChecks.test_help.summary:
Both entry scripts must terminate successfully after printing help,
